title: Bond Basics
description: Understand face value, stated rate, market rate, maturity and bond cash flows.
html:
What is a bond?

A bond is a form of long-term borrowing. The issuer receives cash from investors and promises to make specified payments.

Important bond terms

Face Value: Amount repaid at maturity.

Stated or Coupon Rate: Rate used to determine periodic cash interest payments.

Market or Effective Rate: Rate investors demand when the bond is issued.

Maturity Date: Date the face amount is repaid.

Cash interest

Cash Interest = Face Value × Stated Rate × Time

Example

A company has $100,000 of bonds with a 6% annual stated rate.

$100,000 × 6% = $6,000 Annual Cash Interest

Semiannual payments

If the bond pays interest twice each year:

$100,000 × 6% × 6/12 = $3,000

The company pays $3,000 every six months.

Stated rate vs market rate

These rates are not the same thing.

Stated Rate

Determines the contractual cash interest payment.

Market Rate

Helps determine the bond's issue price and effective yield.

The relationship we'll use next

  • Stated rate = market rate → generally issued near face value
  • Stated rate < market rate → generally issued at a discount
  • Stated rate > market rate → generally issued at a premium

Why?

If investors can earn 8% elsewhere but your bond pays only 6%, they generally will not pay full face value for it.

The issue price must fall so the investor's effective yield becomes competitive with the market.

quiz.prompt: A $200,000 bond has a 5% annual stated rate and pays interest semiannually. How much cash interest is paid every six months?
